speaker: Doctor
text: I am sorry to hear you are dealing with acute diarrhea; to begin our evaluation, have you had any recent travel, and have you been eating any foods that others who ate with you have also consumed? Additionally, have you experienced fever, blood in your stool, or severe abdominal pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Clostridioides difficile infection (C. diff colitis).

Given your recent treatment with levofloxacin and the onset of watery diarrhea with abdominal cramping, I strongly suspect antibiotic-associated colitis. Please proceed with a stool PCR test for C. difficile toxins immediately.
